question:
(i) What is ionisation energy of hydrogen atom in the ground state?
(ii) Why is this energy equal to $13.6\text{ eV}$?

options.A:
(i) The ionisation energy from ground state is $0\text{ eV}$.
(ii) The ground state energy is already zero.
options.B:
(i) The ionisation energy is $-13.6\text{ eV}$.
(ii) Ionisation means the electron moves to a more negative-energy state.
options.C:
(i) The ionisation energy is $27.2\text{ eV}$.
(ii) It is twice the ground-state energy.
options.D:
(i) Ionisation energy is the minimum energy required to remove the electron from ground state to infinity.
(ii) Since $E_1=-13.6\text{ eV}$ and $E_\infty=0$, $\Delta E=0-(-13.6)=13.6\text{ eV}$.
